title: Self-organized Layered Structures of Nitrogen-Vacancy Centers with Preferential Orientation in Heteroepitaxial Diamond Films
authors: Vadim Lebedev, Alejandro Martínez-Méndez, Jesús Moreno-Meseguer, Jan Engels, Jürgen Weippert, Jan Kustermann, Felix Hoffmann, Javier Prior, Jan Jeske
abstract: Here, we report the fabrication and characterization of single crystal diamond films on a two-inch wafer-scale containing three-dimensional layered structures of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy color centers (NV$^{-}$). The (100)-oriented layered diamond films were grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) to create spatially separated regions of enhanced emission associated with NV$^{-}$ centers. Such localized emission enhancement as well as 2D and 3D arrays of spins could enable close-packed architectures for emerging quantum devices, such as data processors, memory cells, and magnetic sensors. A cyclic sequence of CVD growth and oxygen-plasma etching is employed, resulting in the in-situ formation of layered inverted pyramidal structures with flat $\{$111$\}$ sidewalls. These pits are subsequently overgrown by nitrogen-doped diamond to achieve NV$^{-}$-rich facets with a uniform N-V bond arrangement and improved nitrogen incorporation efficiency.
summary: This work reports the fabrication of wafer-scale diamond films featuring highly ordered, layered structures of $	ext{NV}^-$ centers. By using a cyclic etching/growth process, the researchers achieved preferential alignment of these quantum emitters along specific crystal facets. This controlled patterning is crucial for developing integrated, addressable solid-state quantum devices.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fabrication and characterization of diamond films containing highly ordered, three-dimensional layered structures of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy color centers ($	ext{NV}^-$) on a wafer scale.
main_result: A cyclic CVD growth and etching process successfully creates $	ext{NV}^-$-rich micro-clusters with preferential, uniform alignment of $	ext{NV}$ pairs along the [111] direction, enabling scalable quantum architectures.
method: The authors employed a cyclic process involving Chemical Vapor Deposition ($	ext{CVD}$) and oxygen-plasma etching, followed by advanced characterization using $	ext{ODMR}$, $	ext{cPL}$, and $	ext{CL}$ spectroscopy.
model_or_system: The physical system is the diamond lattice hosting $	ext{NV}^-$ color centers. The methodology relies on controlling crystal growth anisotropy by etching to create $\{111\}$-bounded pits, which are then overgrown to enhance $	ext{NV}$ concentration and alignment.
key_observables: Photoluminescence ($	ext{PL}$) map showing $	ext{ZPL}$ at $637 	ext{ nm}$; Optically Detected Magnetic Resonance ($	ext{ODMR}$) confirming preferential alignment; Coherence time ($T_2$) measured at $34.6 \pm 2.5 \mu	ext{s}$.
important_parameters: Wafer scale (two-inch), $	ext{NV}^-$ state, $\{111\}$ facet orientation, and the cyclic $	ext{CVD}$ growth parameters.
main_assumptions: The enhanced $	ext{NV}^-$ emission originates specifically from the inclined $\{111\}$ sidewalls formed during the etching/overgrowth cycle, which dictates the alignment.
figures_summary: Figures show $	ext{PL}$ maps indicating layered structures, cross-sections confirming $\{111\}$-bounded pits, and $	ext{ODMR}$ spectra demonstrating four complementary regions of $	ext{NV}$ alignment.
paper_structure: The paper details the fabrication process using cyclic $	ext{CVD}$ to create 3D layered structures. It then characterizes these structures using $	ext{SEM}$, $	ext{cPL}$, and $	ext{ODMR}$ to prove the preferential alignment of $	ext{NV}$ centers along the [111] direction, culminating in discussions of potential quantum device applications.
why_interesting: The precise, controlled engineering of solid-state quantum emitters ($	ext{NV}^-$) in a scalable, patterned manner is highly relevant to quantum information science, offering a platform for solid-state qubits and quantum memory.
